questions.stem:
Three forces $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$ act on a particle $P$.
$\mathbf{F}_1 = (2\mathbf{i} + 3a\mathbf{j})$ N; $\mathbf{F}_2 = (2a\mathbf{i} + b\mathbf{j})$ N; $\mathbf{F}_3 = (b\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j})$ N.
The particle $P$ is in equilibrium under the action of these forces.

parts.text:
Find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
$(2\mathbf{i}+3a\mathbf{j})+(2a\mathbf{i}+b\mathbf{j})+(b\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}) = \mathbf{0}$ M1: Use of resultant force = 0 (seen or implied)
$2a+b+2=0$; $3a+b+4=0$ M1: In an equation involving all three forces once and once only, compare $\mathbf{i}$ or $\mathbf{j}$ components to form an equation in $a$ and $b$. Allow with $\mathbf{i}$ or $\mathbf{j}$. $\lambda\mathbf{i}=\mu\mathbf{j}$ is M0
A1: Two correct scalar equations. No i/j
$a=-2; b=2$ DM1: Solve simultaneous equations to find $a$ or $b$. Dependent on the previous M1
A1: $a$ correct
A1: $b$ correct

questions.stem:
Figure 1
A particle $P$ of mass 2 kg is pushed by a constant horizontal force of magnitude 30 N up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane. The plane is inclined to the horizontal at an angle $\alpha$, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$, as shown in Figure 1. The line of action of the force lies in the vertical plane containing $P$ and the line of greatest slope of the plane. The particle $P$ starts from rest. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is $\mu$. After 2 seconds, $P$ has travelled a distance of 5.5 m up the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the acceleration of $P$ up the plane.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$5.5=\frac{1}{2}a.2^2$ M1: Complete method using suvat equations to form an equation in $a$ only
$\Rightarrow a=2.75$ A1

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
$R=30\sin\alpha+2g\cos\alpha$ M1: Resolve perpendicular to the plane to find an expression for $R$. Must have all terms. Condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion.
A2: -1 each error. All correct A1A1, one error A1A0, two or more errors A0A0 ($R=33.68$)
$-F+30\cos\alpha-2g\sin\alpha=2a$ M1: Equation of motion parallel to the plane with $a$ or their $a$. Must have all terms. Condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion.
A2: -1 each error ($F=6.74$)
$\mu=\frac{30\cos\alpha-2g\sin\alpha-5.5}{30\sin\alpha+2g\cos\alpha}$ DM1: Use $F=\mu R$. Dependent on the 2 previous M marks
$=0.200$ or $0.20$ A1: Do not accept 0.2

parts.text:
A small stone is released from rest from a point $A$ which is at height $h$ metres above horizontal ground. Exactly one second later another small stone is projected with speed 19.6 m s$^{-1}$ vertically downwards from a point $B$, which is also at height $h$ metres above the horizontal ground. The motion of each stone is modelled as that of a particle moving freely under gravity. The two stones hit the ground at the same time.
Find the value of $h$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use $s=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^2$ or a complete suvat route to find $h$ in terms of $t$
$h=\frac{1}{2}gt^2$ A1: Or $h=\frac{1}{2}g(t+1)^2$. The expression for time used in the first equation defines the expression expected in the second equation.
$h=19.6(t-1)+\frac{1}{2}g(t-1)^2$ A1: Or $h=19.6(t)+\frac{1}{2}g(t)^2$ or $h=4.9+(9.8t+\frac{1}{2}gt^2)$
$\frac{1}{2}gt^2=19.6(t-1)+\frac{1}{2}g(t-1)^2$ M1: Equate the two expressions for $h$.
DM1: Solve for $t$. Dependent on the previous M1.
$t=1.5$ A1: Using the "Or" approach gives $t=0.5$
$h=11$ m or 11.0 m A1: Accept 2 or 3 s.f. only

questions.stem: A car travelling along a straight horizontal road takes 170 s to travel between two sets of traffic lights at $A$ and $B$ which are 2125 m apart. The car starts from rest at $A$ and moves with constant acceleration until it reaches a speed of 17 m s$^{-1}$. The car then maintains this speed before moving with constant deceleration, coming to rest at $B$. The magnitude of the deceleration is twice the magnitude of the acceleration.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Sketch, in the space below, a speed-time graph for the motion of the car between $A$ and $B$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: shape
B1: rel grad - RHS steeper than LHS
B1: 17 and 170 shown

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the deceleration of the car.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
$T;2T$ B1: Correct ratios of times for acceleration and deceleration seen or implied.
$\frac{170+(170-3T)}{2}17=2125$ Or $\frac{1}{2}\times T_1\times17+17(170-(T_1+T_2))+\frac{1}{2}\times17\times T_2=2125$ Or $2125=\frac{17}{2}(170+T')$ M1: Form an equation for total distance with their times
A2: -1 each error
$T=30$ Or $T_1+T_2=90$ A1: Use their equation and the correct ratio to find the value for time decelerating or the total of time accelerating and decelerating
M1: Use of $v=u+at$ or equivalent
decel $=\frac{17}{30}$ oe A1: $(0.56\dot{})$ 3sf or better. Must be positive.

questions.stem:
Figure 2
A plank $AB$ has length 4 m and mass 6 kg. The plank rests in a horizontal position on two supports, one at $B$ and one at $C$, where $AC=1.5$ m. A load of mass 15 kg is placed on the plank at the point $X$, as shown in Figure 2, and the plank remains horizontal and in equilibrium. The plank is modelled as a uniform rod and the load is modelled as a particle. The magnitude of the reaction on the plank at $C$ is twice the magnitude of the reaction on the plank at $B$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the magnitude of the reaction on the plank at $C$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Resolve vertically to form an equation in $R_C$ or $R_D$. All terms required. Condone sign errors.
$2T+T=6g+15g$ A1: Correct unsimplified equation ($R+\frac{1}{2}R=6g+15g$)
$2T=14g=137$ N or 140 N A1

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Take moments - all terms must be present and of the correct structure. Form an equation with one unknown length.
$M(A)$: $15g\cdot AX+6g\times2=(2T\times1.5)+4T=7T$
$M(B)$: $15gd+6g\times2=2T\times2.5$
$M(c\ of\ m)$: $2T\times0.5+15gd=2\times T$
$M(C)$: $6g\times0.5+15g(x-1.5)=T\times2.5$
A2: -1 each error. Follow their $T$. NB: Use of the correct reactions the wrong way round is one error. ($15g\approx147$, $6g\approx58.8$, $12g\approx117.6$)
M1: Substitute for $T$ and solve for $AX$
$AX=\frac{37}{15}$ m = 2.5 m (or better) A1: $2.4\dot{6}$
NB: If you see parts (a) and (b) merged, award the 8 marks as bM1 for the first moments equation, bA2 for the equation correct, aM1 for a second moments equation and an attempt to solve for $R_C$, aA1 for the second equation correct, aA1 for the reaction correct, bM1 and bA1 as above

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The load is now moved along the plank to a point $Y$, between $A$ and $C$. Given that the plank is on the point of tipping about $C$,
(c) find the distance $AY$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
$M(C)$: $15g\cdot YC=6g\times0.5$ M1: Requires both terms present and of the correct structure. No additional terms (Using $R_C=21g$, $R_B=0$)
A1: Correct unsimplified equation
$YC=0.2$ m A1
$AY=1.3$ m A1
Alt (c): $M(A)$: $15gAY+6g\times2=1.5\times21g$ M1: Requires all terms present and of the correct structure. No additional terms
A2: Correct unsimplified equation -1 each error
$AY=1.3$ m A1
Alt (c): $M(C)$: $6g\times0.5=15g(1.5-AY)$ M1
A2: -1 each error
$AY=1.3$ m A1

questions.notes: [ms_verify] (a) '$R_C$ or $R_B$' -> '$R_C$ or $R_D$' (MS p.11: Page shows R_c or R_D in the part (a) M1 note, not R_B)

parts.text:
A particle $P$ moves from point $A$ to point $B$ with constant acceleration $(c\mathbf{i}+d\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-2}$, where $c$ and $d$ are positive constants. The velocity of $P$ at $A$ is $(-3\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-1}$ and the velocity of $P$ at $B$ is $(2\mathbf{i}+9\mathbf{j})$ m s$^{-1}$. The magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ is 2.6 m s$^{-2}$.
Find the value of $c$ and the value of $d$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$(2\mathbf{i}+9\mathbf{j})-(-3\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})$ M1: Use of $\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}(=\mathbf{a}t)$ seen or implied
$=(5\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})$ A1
$k^2(5^2+12^2)=2.6^2$ ($k=1/t$) M1: Use magnitude $=2.6=k|\mathbf{a}|$ (linking 2.6 & 13)
$c=5\times0.2=1$ A1
$d=12\times0.2=2.4$ A1

questions.stem:
Figure 3
Two particles $P$ and $Q$ have masses $m$ and $4m$ respectively. The particles are attached to the ends of a light inextensible string. Particle $P$ is held at rest on a rough horizontal table. The string lies along the table and passes over a small smooth light pulley which is fixed at the edge of the table. Particle $Q$ hangs at rest vertically below the pulley, at a height $h$ above a horizontal plane, as shown in Figure 3. The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the table is 0.5. Particle $P$ is released from rest with the string taut and slides along the table.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find, in terms of $mg$, the tension in the string while both particles are moving.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
$R=mg$ B1: Forces acting vertically on $P$
$F=0.5R$ B1: Use of $F=\mu R$
M1: One equation of motion. Requires all terms but condone sign errors
$4mg-T=\pm4ma$ A1
M1: A second equation of motion of $P$. Requires all terms but condone sign errors
$T-F=\pm ma$ A1: Signs of $a$ must be consistent
Condone use of $4mg-F=5ma$ in place of either of the above equations.
$4mg-0.5mg=5ma$ or $4mg-T=4T-2mg$, $a=0.7g$ DDM1: Solve for $T$. Dependent on the two preceding M marks
$T=1.2mg$ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The particle $P$ does not reach the pulley before $Q$ hits the plane.
(b) Show that the speed of $Q$ immediately before it hits the plane is $\sqrt{1.4gh}$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$v^2=2\times0.7gh$ M1: Complete method to an equation in $v$ or $v^2$
$v=\sqrt{1.4gh}$ A1: Obtain given answer or exact equivalent from exact working with no errors seen.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
When $Q$ hits the plane, $Q$ does not rebound and $P$ continues to slide along the table. Given that $P$ comes to rest before it reaches the pulley,
(c) show that the total length of the string must be greater than $2.4h$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
$-0.5mg=ma'$ M1: Complete method to find the deceleration of $P$
$\Rightarrow a'=-0.5g$ A1
M1: Complete method to find additional distance in terms of $h$ ($a\neq0.7g, a\neq g$)
$0^2=1.4gh-2\times0.5g\times d$ A1: Correctly substituted equation. Follow their $a\neq0.7g, a\neq g$.
$d=1.4h$ A1
Hence, length of string is greater than $1.4h+h=2.4h$ A1: Obtain given answer with no errors seen. Their statement needs to reflect the inequality.
